title: Controlled Reliability-Shift Test of Risk-Monotone Counterfactual Fusion
research_question: Does learned normalized fusion with counterfactual consistency and disagreement-conditioned intrinsic risk outperform parameter-matched uniform fusion under controlled source-disjoint reliability shifts?
current_hypothesis: The full mechanism improves clean accuracy and corrupted selective accuracy while preserving host-risk and transition invariants.
scope: Synthetic controlled-mechanism evidence only; external validity and JEPA claims excluded.

datasets.scientific_role: future external visual intervention and JEPA candidate

claims.claim: The registered mechanism improves both primary endpoints within the controlled generator.
The implemented effective risk never falls below host risk.
The result establishes natural-data or JEPA performance.

decisions: Versioned as a successor because the predecessor lacks admissible aligned natural data.
Synthetic evidence cannot close the predecessor's real-data question.
Protocol frozen before generator execution or outcome inspection.
The 50-percent selective endpoint was clarified before scientific freeze and protected inspection.
Resource and workload locks were never weakened.
The negative outcome is terminal for this hypothesis; any reliability-supervised router is a new successor.
The separately versioned v3 reliability-supervised successor was executed and also terminated NEGATIVE; v2 evidence was not rewritten.

failures.result: A duplicate campaign invocation encountered the workload lock and produced retained invalid lock-contention receipts; no protected outcome was opened.
The full learned mechanism failed both registered primary superiority criteria.
